deep.reconstruction:
Context: this sheet is not an autograph working page. It is a copy of Riemann's letter to Weierstrass, printed posthumously as "Beweis des Satzes, dass eine einwerthige mehr als 2n-fach periodische Function von n Veränderlichen unmöglich ist" (Borchardt's/Crelle's Journal 71, 1870). Riemann's argument starts on this page and continues on the next.

Setting. Let f(x), with x = (x_1,...,x_n) in C^n, be single-valued. It has 2n period vectors a_mu = (a_mu^1,...,a_mu^n), mu = 1..2n, meaning f(x + a_mu) = f(x).

Step 1 (real coordinates). Identify C^n with R^{2n}. If the 2n vectors a_mu are linearly independent over R, every x can be written uniquely as x_nu = sum_{mu=1}^{2n} a_mu^nu xi_mu (nu = 1..n) with real xi_mu. Taking real and imaginary parts gives 2n real linear equations in the 2n unknowns xi. Riemann's footnote ** says the representation needs exactly this independence. He also says the exceptional cases are easy to handle.

Step 2 (fundamental domain). Let P = { sum a_mu xi_mu : 0 <= xi_mu < 1 }, one endpoint excluded. Every x is congruent modulo the lattice Lambda = Z a_1 + ... + Z a_{2n} to exactly one point of P. Riemann calls P "das bei diesen 2n Modulsystemen periodisch sich wiederholende Grössengebiet" (the period parallelotope).

Step 3 (an extra period). Suppose a_{2n+1} is also a period and is not in Lambda.
- Take the points x + k a_{2n+1}, k in Z, and reduce each modulo Lambda to a point y_k in P.
- All y_k are congruent to each other modulo the 2n+1 periods, so f takes the same value at all of them.
- Case (a): the y_k are pairwise distinct. Then P contains arbitrarily many (infinitely many) such points.
- Case (b): y_k = y_l for some k != l. Then (k - l) a_{2n+1} is in Lambda. This gives integer relations sum_{mu=1}^{2n+1} m_mu a_mu^nu = 0 (nu = 1..n) with m_{2n+1} != 0. Riemann promises to show later that the 2n+1 period systems can then be generated by just 2n of them.

[Continuation on the next page, summarised for context.]
- Case (a): divide each xi-interval into q equal parts, so P splits into q^{2n} cells. Among more than q^{2n} mutually congruent points, two fall in the same cell (pigeonhole). So f is invariant under a nonzero translation whose xi-coordinates all have size at most 1/q. Letting q go to infinity, a continuous f is invariant under arbitrarily small translations. Riemann concludes that f is a function of fewer than n linear combinations of the x, i.e. it is degenerate.
- Case (b): a gcd/Bezout reduction. With theta = gcd(m_1, m_2) and beta m_1 - alpha m_2 = theta, set c_1 = (m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2)/theta and b = alpha a_1 + beta a_2. Then a_1 = beta c_1 - (m_2/theta) b and a_2 = -alpha c_1 + (m_1/theta) b, so the pair (c_1, b) generates the same group as (a_1, a_2). Iterating this completes a primitive vector to a basis, a unimodular completion.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The relation obtained in case (b) consists of n complex equations, i.e. 2n real ones. Riemann writes 'n Gleichungen', which is correct when they are read as complex equations.

Unjustified on this page (deferred by Riemann): case (b) only gives (k-l) a_{2n+1} in Lambda, i.e. a_{2n+1} lies in (1/N)Lambda. That the group generated is then again a lattice with 2n generators is promised 'später' and proved on the next page by the gcd reduction.

Footnote **: the case where the 2n periods are R-dependent is called easy but is not treated. In that case the periods do not form a lattice of full rank and the function is degenerate or has infinitesimal periods. The claim is plausible but not argued here.

The overall theorem silently assumes continuity (it is stated explicitly on the next page) and non-degeneracy. Strictly, 'impossible' should read 'impossible unless f depends on fewer than n linear combinations of the variables'. The next page states this correctly.

results.what: A single-valued (continuous, non-degenerate) function of n complex variables cannot have more than 2n independent periods. Proof via a fundamental parallelotope and reduction of multiples of an extra period.
results.modern_name: Bound on the rank of the period group, i.e. discrete subgroups of R^{2n} are lattices of rank <= 2n (generalised Jacobi theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1834/35) for n=1; Riemann (letter to Weierstrass c. 1859, published 1870 in Crelle 71) and Weierstrass for general n

results.what: Every point is congruent modulo 2n R-independent periods to exactly one point of the half-open parallelotope 0 <= xi_mu < 1.
results.modern_name: Fundamental domain of a lattice in C^n = R^{2n}

results.what: Dichotomy for an extra period: either infinitely many distinct congruent points in the fundamental domain, or an integer relation among the 2n+1 periods.
results.modern_name: Kronecker-type dichotomy (dense orbit vs. torsion modulo a lattice)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copy of Riemann's well-known letter to Weierstrass, published in Crelle 71 (1870) and included in his Werke. The theorem and proof method are standard and already attributed to him. The page holds nothing unpublished.

checkable.sympy: a1,a2,m1,m2,al,be,th=symbols('a1 a2 m1 m2 al be th'); c1=(a1*m1+a2*m2)/th; b=al*a1+be*a2; simplify((be*c1-(m2/th)*b - a1).subs(th, be*m1-al*m2))
checkable.asserts: The gcd reduction (next page) recovers a_1: the result is 0 when theta = beta*m1 - alpha*m2.

checkable.asserts: The gcd reduction recovers a_2, so (c1, b) generates the same group as (a1, a2).

checkable.sympy: Matrix([[1,0],[0,1]]).det() != 0  # for n=1, periods 1 and I as real vectors (1,0),(0,1)
checkable.asserts: Unique real coordinates xi exist when the realified 2n x 2n period matrix is nonsingular (the condition in footnote **).

checkable.sympy: import math; q=3; n=1; N=q**(2*n)+1; N > q**(2*n)
checkable.asserts: Pigeonhole step (next page): more than q^{2n} points in q^{2n} cells force two into the same cell.

transcription_corrections: Header: the page is a copy of the published letter (it cites Borchardt's Journal Bd. 71 and footnote *: 'Auszug aus einem Schreiben Riemann's an Hrn. Weierstrass'). It is not an autograph working sheet.
'ich theile [-?-] Ihnen' : the struck item appears to be a deleted false start of 'Ihnen'. Reading: 'ich theile Ihnen daher hier noch einmal mit.'
'Grössen[-gebiets-]systeme' : correct, 'gebiets' is struck out, giving 'einem Grössensysteme'.
Footnote **, last words: the image is faint. It probably reads 'die Ausnahmen sind aber leicht zu behandeln', which is consistent with the printed text.
